extraFacts.fact: A hose or tube size code is in sixteenths of an inch: 02 is 1/8 inch, 03 is 3/16 inch, 04 is 1/4 inch, 05 is 5/16 inch, 06 is 3/8 inch, 08 is 1/2 inch, 10 is 5/8 inch, 12 is 3/4 inch, 14 is 7/8 inch and 16 is 1 inch.
extraFacts.source: SAE J517 / SAE J1131 dash-size convention used across brass fitting makers

extraFacts.fact: Brass tube fittings, couplings and hose barbs are normally classified under HS subheading 7412.20 (copper-alloy tube or pipe fittings); the importer's customs broker has the final say.

ISO 7-1 covers pipe threads where the pressure-tight joint is made on the thread, such as the BSP taper (R) thread; ISO 228-1 covers pipe threads where the joint is not made on the thread, such as the BSP parallel (G) thread; ASME B1.20.1 is the general-purpose NPT pipe thread standard; ASME B1.20.3 covers Dryseal pipe threads, including NPTF; SAE J512 covers automotive tube fittings including flareless compression.
extraFacts.source: ISO 7-1, ISO 228-1, ASME B1.20.1, ASME B1.20.3, SAE J512

extraFacts.fact: SAE J2494 covers push-to-connect fittings for air brake tubing and FMVSS 571.106 covers brake hoses and their end fittings; the maker of the DOT push-in fittings states compliance with both. SAE J844 covers nonmetallic air brake tubing. DOT-approved air brake fittings are for compressed-air brake systems.
extraFacts.source: SAE J2494, SAE J844, FMVSS 571.106 (as stated on the listing)

faqs.q: What is the Brass Compression Nut used for?
faqs.a: The Brass Compression Nut is a compression nut in brass for flareless compression tube joints on a wide variety of tubing. The listing has 10 part numbers, 1/8" to 7/8" tube.

faqs.q: How do I read the part number IH-BR-61-07 on the Brass Compression Nut?
faqs.a: The base number IH-BR-61 is followed by one code per end, each a size in sixteenths of an inch. Here 07 is 7/16" tube, compression. The same rule holds on every row of this listing, so IH-BR-61-02 is 1/8" tube, compression.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Brass Compression Nut come in?
faqs.a: The Brass Compression Nut has 10 part numbers, 1/8" to 7/8" tube. For example IH-BR-61-02, IH-BR-61-06, IH-BR-61-14 (1/8" tube, compression to 7/8" tube, compression).

faqs.q: How do I pick the right size of the Brass Compression Nut?
faqs.a: Match the tube size to the tube end, which is the outside diameter of the tube in inches, and the thread size to the port on a threaded end. For example IH-BR-61-07 is 7/16" tube, compression. Check the thread form on the port before ordering; our [guide on what to send for a fittings quote](/blog/what-to-send-for-a-fittings-quote) lists what helps.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature is the Brass Compression Nut rated for?
faqs.a: The manufacturer publishes no pressure rating for this family, so there is no figure to quote for the Brass Compression Nut. Tell us the medium, working pressure and temperature and we confirm the fitting before you order.

faqs.q: What is the Brass Compression Nut made of?
faqs.a: The body is brass. Brass suits air, water and fuel lines but not strong acids or ammonia. Ask us if you need another metal for the Brass Compression Nut.

faqs.q: Which standards does the Brass Compression Nut follow?
faqs.a: The listing names SAE J512 for the Brass Compression Nut. SAE J512 covers automotive tube fittings, including flareless compression. Say which certificate or declaration you need and we ask the maker what it can supply.

faqs.q: What does the Brass Compression Nut connect to?
faqs.a: The Brass Compression Nut connects to tube cut square, such as copper or brass tube, or plastic tube with a tube insert. Matching parts are on our [brass compression fittings](/c/brass-compression-fittings) shelf.

faqs.q: How should the Brass Compression Nut be installed?
faqs.a: For the Brass Compression Nut, cut the tube square, slide on the nut and sleeve, seat the tube and tighten the nut so the sleeve is squeezed onto it, which makes the seal without a flare. Use a tube insert in plastic tube; our [guide to brass flare and compression fittings](/blog/brass-flare-and-compression-fittings) explains flare and compression joints.

faqs.q: How does the Brass Compression Nut differ from Brass Compression Nut, Long?
faqs.a: They are neighbouring parts on the same shelf with different ends or body: the Brass Compression Nut is a compression nut in brass. See [Brass Compression Nut, Long](/p/brass-compression-nut-long) for the other and pick by the ends your line needs.

faqs.q: What is the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee used for?
faqs.a: The Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee is a adapter tee in brass for flareless compression tube joints on a wide variety of tubing. Its ends are NPTF (Dryseal) female, NPTF (Dryseal) male and compression tube end. The listing has 2 part numbers, 1/8".

faqs.q: How do I read the part number IH-BR-376-02-02-04 on the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee?
faqs.a: The base number IH-BR-376 is followed by one code per end, each a size in sixteenths of an inch. Here 02 is 1/8" NPTF, 02 is 1/8" NPTF, 04 is 1/4" tube, compression. The same rule holds on every row of this listing, so IH-BR-376-02-02-03 is 1/8" NPTF (1/8-27) x 1/8" NPTF (1/8-27) x 3/16" tube, compression.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee come in?
faqs.a: The Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee has 2 part numbers, 1/8". For example IH-BR-376-02-02-03, IH-BR-376-02-02-04 (1/8" NPTF (1/8-27) x 1/8" NPTF (1/8-27) x 3/16" tube, compression to 1/8" NPTF (1/8-27) x 1/8" NPTF (1/8-27) x 1/4" tube, compression). End 1: NPTF (Dryseal), 1/8" (1/8-27); End 2: NPTF (Dryseal), 1/8" (1/8-27); End 3: compression tube end, 3/16" to 1/4".

faqs.q: How do I pick the right size of the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee?
faqs.a: Match the tube size to the tube end, which is the outside diameter of the tube in inches, and the thread size to the port on a threaded end. For example IH-BR-376-02-02-04 is 1/8" NPTF (1/8-27) x 1/8" NPTF (1/8-27) x 1/4" tube, compression. Check the thread form on the port before ordering; our [guide on what to send for a fittings quote](/blog/what-to-send-for-a-fittings-quote) lists what helps.

faqs.q: What is the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee made of?
faqs.a: The body is brass. Brass suits air, water and fuel lines but not strong acids or ammonia. Ask us if you need another metal for the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee.

faqs.q: Which standards does the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee follow?
faqs.a: The listing names ASME B1.20.3, SAE J512 for the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee. ASME B1.20.3 covers Dryseal pipe threads, including NPTF. SAE J512 covers automotive tube fittings, including flareless compression. Say which certificate or declaration you need and we ask the maker what it can supply.

faqs.q: What does the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee connect to?
faqs.a: The Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee connects to a male NPT or NPTF pipe nipple, plug or adapter. On its other end it takes a female NPT or NPTF port, such as a valve, tank or manifold port. Matching parts are on our [brass NPTF pipe fittings](/c/brass-nptf-pipe-fittings) shelf.

faqs.q: How should the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee be installed?
faqs.a: For the Brass NPTF Female × NPTF Male × Compression Tee, cut the tube square, slide on the nut and sleeve, seat the tube and tighten the nut so the sleeve is squeezed onto it, which makes the seal without a flare. Use a tube insert in plastic tube; our [guide to brass flare and compression fittings](/blog/brass-flare-and-compression-fittings) explains flare and compression joints.
